Kodely writes a real Vite + React + TypeScript site, shows a live preview, and publishes it to a free URL in one click.","targetKeyword":"ai website generator from a description","category":"Feature","bodyHtml":"

Most so-called AI website generators take a sentence and hand back a template with your headline swapped in. Kodely takes a sentence and hands back a real codebase: a Vite + React 19 + TypeScript app styled with Tailwind CSS v4, built on hand-built UI primitives instead of a page builder's div soup. You describe the site once, in plain English, and an actual application gets written, compiled, and rendered in front of you.

That distinction matters because it determines what happens next. A template swap is a dead end — you can change colors and text, not structure. A real codebase is something you can keep talking to. Ask for a new section, a different layout, a pricing table, and Kodely edits the actual component files, not a config blob pretending to be one.

The core idea: one sentence in, a real site out

You open Kodely, type a description of the site you want, and the AI scaffolds it from a real foundation codebase — not a blank file, not raw HTML strings. Every project starts with working UI primitives already in place, so the first response is a functioning app, not a wireframe. From there, the site is yours to keep shaping through the same chat interface.

How it works: describe, preview, publish

The flow has three steps, and none of them involve touching a file tree.

  1. Describe. Tell Kodely what the site is for and who it's for, in as much or as little detail as you have. It reads the request and starts generating real .tsx components.
  2. Preview. As the app is built, you're watching the actual compiled result — the same React app that would run in production — not a static mockup standing in for one.
  3. Publish. One click puts the site live at a free public URL on the *.kodely.site domain. No hosting setup, no deploy step to configure. It's just live.

After that, revisions work the same way changes always work in Kodely: you describe what you want changed, and it edits the real components behind the preview.

A real example: describe to site

Say you type: A one-page site for a mobile dog-walking business in Austin. Need a hero with a booking button, a services section listing walks and drop-in visits, pricing, and a contact form.

Kodely reads that and generates a real component tree: a hero component with a call-to-action button wired to scroll to a booking section, a services grid built from reusable card components, a pricing section pulling from the same design system as the rest of the app, and a contact form with working input state. You see all of this compile and render in the live preview within moments — not a screenshot of what it might look like, the actual app.

From there you keep going conversationally: make the hero background darker, add a testimonials section above pricing, change the booking button to say Get a Free Quote. Each request edits the real files. If a generation fails to compile, Kodely attempts one automatic repair before it ever reaches you — and a build that still fails to compile is never charged against your credits.

Proof points

Three things separate this from a template-and-swap tool:

What you getWhy it matters
Real, inspectable codeEvery generated file is a real .tsx component you can open and read in-app. Nothing is hidden behind a proprietary renderer.
Publish-time secret scanningBefore any site goes live, Kodely scans it for accidentally leaked API keys or secrets so a careless prompt doesn't ship a credential to the public internet.
One-click live URLPublishing isn't a separate hosting step you have to configure. It's built into the same click, and the resulting *.kodely.site URL is free and included.

There's also a safety net built into the generation process itself: every successful build is a checkpoint. If a change takes the site somewhere you don't like, rolling back to an earlier checkpoint is free and instant.

Honest scope: what Kodely doesn't do yet

Kodely is a frontend generator today, and it's worth being direct about the edges. There's no backend, database, authentication, or payment processing generated — what you get is a real, complete frontend application. Sites currently publish only to a *.kodely.site subdomain; custom domains aren't supported yet. Editing happens through chat, not a click-to-edit visual canvas. And while you can see and copy every generated source file in-app, there's no zip export or download yet. If your project needs a login system or a database today, Kodely isn't the tool for that step — but for getting a real, working, publishable frontend out of a description, it's built exactly for that.

Pricing in plain terms

Sign up and you get 750 credits free, no credit card required. Credits are metered against real AI cost, so a heavier generation costs more than a small tweak — and again, anything that fails to compile isn't charged. When you need more, top-ups are straightforward: $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits (the most popular option), or $90 for 6,000 credits. Credits never expire, so there's no pressure to burn them before a reset date. See the full breakdown on the pricing page.

FAQ

Is the generated site a real app or a template?

Real app. Kodely writes actual Vite + React 19 + TypeScript components styled with Tailwind CSS v4, starting from a hand-built foundation codebase. It's not a template with placeholder text swapped in.

Can I see the code it generates?

Yes. Every generated file is viewable and copyable in-app. There's no zip export yet, but nothing is hidden from you.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. The entire flow — from first description to published site to every revision after — happens through plain-English chat.

What does publishing cost?

Nothing. Publishing to your *.kodely.site URL is free and included; you're only spending credits on generation.

Can I use my own domain?

Not yet. Today every published site lives on a *.kodely.site subdomain.

What happens if a generation fails?

Kodely automatically attempts one repair. If it still fails to compile, you aren't charged credits for it.

If you've got a real site in your head and a sentence to describe it, that's the whole input Kodely needs. Start building free and watch it compile in front of you — or compare the approach on the Kodely vs. Lovable breakdown first.

The core idea: one sentence in, a real site out

You open Kodely, type a description of the site you want, and the AI scaffolds it from a real foundation codebase — not a blank file, not raw HTML strings. Every project starts with working UI primitives already in place, so the first response is a functioning app, not a wireframe.

How it works: describe, preview, publish

The flow has three steps, and none of them involve touching a file tree.

  1. Describe. Tell Kodely what the site is for and who it's for, in as much or as little detail as you have. It reads the request and starts generating real .tsx components.
  2. Preview. As the app is built, you're watching the actual compiled result — the same React app that would run in production — not a static mockup standing in for one.
  3. Publish. One click puts the site live at a free public URL on the *.kodely.site domain. No hosting setup, no deploy step to configure. It's just live.

Revisions work the same way: you describe what you want changed, and Kodely edits the real components behind the preview.

A real example: describe to site

Say you type: A one-page site for a mobile dog-walking business in Austin. Need a hero with a booking button, a services section listing walks and drop-in visits, pricing, and a contact form.

Kodely generates a real component tree: a hero with a call-to-action wired to scroll to a booking section, a services grid built from reusable cards, a pricing section pulling from the same design system as the rest of the app, and a contact form with working input state. You watch it compile and render in the live preview within moments — the actual app, not a screenshot of what it might look like.

From there you keep going conversationally: make the hero background darker, add a testimonials section above pricing, change the booking button to say Get a Free Quote. If a generation fails to compile, Kodely attempts one automatic repair before it ever reaches you — and a build that still fails to compile is never charged against your credits.

Proof points

Three things separate this from a template-and-swap tool:

What you getWhy it matters
Real, inspectable codeEvery generated file is a real .tsx component you can open and read in-app. Nothing is hidden behind a proprietary renderer.
Publish-time secret scanningBefore any site goes live, Kodely scans it for accidentally leaked API keys or secrets so a careless prompt doesn't ship a credential to the public internet.
One-click live URLPublishing isn't a separate hosting step you have to configure. It's built into the same click, and the resulting *.kodely.site URL is free and included.

There's also a safety net: every successful build is a checkpoint. If a change takes the site somewhere you don't like, rolling back to an earlier checkpoint is free and instant.

Honest scope: what Kodely doesn't do yet

Kodely is a frontend generator today, and it's worth being direct about the edges. There's no backend, database, authentication, or payment processing generated — what you get is a real, complete frontend application. Sites currently publish only to a *.kodely.site subdomain; custom domains aren't supported yet. Editing happens through chat, not a click-to-edit visual canvas. And while you can see and copy every generated source file in-app, there's no zip export or download yet. If your project needs a login system or a database today, Kodely isn't the tool for that step — but for a real, working, publishable frontend out of a description, it's built exactly for that.

Pricing in plain terms

Sign up and you get 750 credits free, no credit card required. Credits are metered against real AI cost, so a heavier generation costs more than a small tweak — and again, anything that fails to compile isn't charged. When you need more, top-ups are straightforward: $9 for 500 credits, $40 for 2,500 credits (the most popular option), or $90 for 6,000 credits. Credits never expire, so there's no pressure to burn them before a reset date. See the full breakdown on the pricing page.

FAQ

Is the generated site a real app or a template?

Real app. Kodely writes actual Vite + React 19 + TypeScript components styled with Tailwind CSS v4, starting from a hand-built foundation codebase. It's not a template with placeholder text swapped in.

Can I see the code it generates?

Yes. Every generated file is viewable and copyable in-app. There's no zip export yet, but nothing is hidden from you.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. The entire flow — from first description to published site to every revision after — happens through plain-English chat.

What does publishing cost?

Nothing. Publishing to your *.kodely.site URL is free and included; you're only spending credits on generation.

Can I use my own domain?

Not yet. Today every published site lives on a *.kodely.site subdomain.

What happens if a generation fails?

Kodely automatically attempts one repair. If it still fails to compile, you aren't charged credits for it.

If you've got a real site in your head and a sentence to describe it, that's the whole input Kodely needs. Start building free and watch it compile in front of you — or compare the approach on the Kodely vs. Lovable breakdown first.
